feeling-depressed-and-hopeless.title: Feeling depressed and hopeless
feeling-depressed-and-hopeless.description: Reflect on how frequently depressive symptoms have impacted your mood, energy, and daily functioning recently.
main_content: Take the first step to recovery
feeling-depressed-and-hopeless.section1_who_content: This assessment is designed for adults 18+.
feeling-depressed-and-hopeless.section2_content:
This assessment helps you reflect on how often low mood, emotional heaviness, or loss of interest has affected you.

It focuses on emotional wellbeing and daily functioning.
feeling-depressed-and-hopeless.section3_subtitle: Understanding your mental health is the first step.
section4_notes: Choose what best describes your experience
feeling-depressed-and-hopeless.metadata.tile1_content:
What is this assessment?

This assessment helps you reflect on how low mood, loss of interest, or emotional heaviness may have been affecting you recently.

It focuses on common experiences such as feeling down, tired, disconnected, or lacking motivation. The goal is not to label you, but to help you notice patterns that may be weighing on your day-to-day life.

What it measures

- Frequency of low mood and loss of interest
- Emotional and physical symptoms linked to depression
- Impact on energy, focus, and daily functioning

Number of questions

- 9 questions

Important
This assessment is not a diagnosis. It is a tool to help you understand whether what you’re experiencing may need attention or support.
feeling-depressed-and-hopeless.metadata.tile2_content:
Abstract, subdued, calming image
(No text · decorative only · aria-hidden)
feeling-depressed-and-hopeless.metadata.tile3_content:
How it works

- Answer based on how you’ve felt over the past 2 weeks
- Choose the option that best matches your experience
- There are no right or wrong answers
- Your progress is saved automatically
- Results appear immediately after completion
feeling-depressed-and-hopeless.metadata.tile4_content:
What you’ll see

After completing the assessment, you’ll see:

- A summary of how often depressive symptoms have appeared
- Clear explanation of what your results may suggest
- Insight into whether symptoms seem occasional or persistent
- Optional next steps such as Equip programs, resources, or professional support

No diagnoses. No labels. Just information to help you decide what to do next.
feeling-depressed-and-hopeless.metadata.tile5_content:
Important notes

- This is a self-help and awareness tool, not a medical diagnosis
- Not intended for emergency or crisis situations
- If you’re feeling unsafe, hopeless, or at risk of harming yourself, seek immediate help from local emergency services or a mental health professional
- You’re encouraged to discuss your results with a qualified professional if helpful
feeling-depressed-and-hopeless.metadata.important_note_1: This is not a medical diagnosis
feeling-depressed-and-hopeless.metadata.important_note_2: If you feel distressed, seek professional support

feeling-overwhelmed-and-anxious.metadata.tile1_content:
What is this assessment?

This assessment helps you understand how anxiety may be showing up in your life right now.

It focuses on common experiences like excessive worrying, restlessness, difficulty relaxing, and feeling on edge. The questions look at how often these experiences have occurred recently—not why they happen.

What it measures

- Frequency of anxiety-related thoughts and sensations
- Impact of worry and tension on daily life
- Whether anxiety feels occasional or persistent

Number of questions

Important
This assessment is not a diagnosis. It helps identify patterns that may be worth paying attention to or discussing further.

What is this assessment?

This assessment helps you understand how stressed or overwhelmed you’ve been feeling lately, and whether life has felt manageable or out of control.

It focuses on how you’ve been responding to everyday pressures—at work, at home, or in your personal life—and how often stress has affected your thoughts and emotions.

- Sense of control vs pressure

feeling-drained-and-burned-out.metadata.tile1_content:
What is this assessment?

This assessment helps you understand whether ongoing demands—especially related to work or responsibilities—may be leading to burnout.

It looks beyond temporary tiredness and focuses on patterns like emotional exhaustion, mental distance, reduced motivation, and difficulty functioning.

What it measures

- Exhaustion and depletion
- Mental distance or disengagement
- Emotional and cognitive strain
- Impact on daily functioning

Number of questions

- 23 questions

Important
This assessment is not a diagnosis. It’s a way to recognize patterns that may signal the need for rest, boundaries, or support.

unsure-or-general-concern.metadata.tile1_content:
What is this assessment?

If you’re not sure what you’re feeling, this assessment helps you pause and take stock.

It brings together short, validated questions related to anxiety, mood, overall well-being, resilience, and confidence. Rather than focusing on one condition, it offers a broad snapshot of your emotional health right now.

What it measures

- General emotional well-being
- Early signs of anxiety or low mood
- Sense of coping, resilience, and self-efficacy

Number of questions

- 11 questions

Important
This assessment is not a diagnosis. It is a starting point to help you understand where you may need attention or support.
unsure-or-general-concern.metadata.tile2_content:
Abstract, calming image
(No text, decorative only)
unsure-or-general-concern.metadata.tile3_content:

- Answer questions based on how you’ve felt recently
- Most questions refer to the past 2 weeks
- There are no right or wrong answers
- Your progress is saved automatically
- You can pause and return anytime
- Results are shown immediately after completion
unsure-or-general-concern.metadata.tile4_content:
What you’ll see

After completing the assessment, you’ll see:

- A simple summary of your responses
- An overview of areas that seem stable and areas that may need attention
- Clear explanations of what your results may indicate
- Suggested next steps such as self-guided tools, Equip programs, or external support resources

No labels. No diagnoses. Just clarity.
unsure-or-general-concern.metadata.tile5_content:
Important notes

- You’re encouraged to share your results with a qualified professional if helpful
